newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SKAARDAL RETAINS SUPER-G TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SKAARDAL RETAINS SUPER-G TITLE.

text.p: Atle Skaardal, competing in his seventh world championships, won the men's super-giant slalom gold medal on Monday to become the first Norwegian to retain an Alpine skiing world title.

The 30-year-old Skaardal, who made his world championship debut in the Italian resort of Bormio in 1985, lived up to his team's nickname of the "Attacking Vikings" and cast aside caution to clock one minute 29.68 seconds.
Compatriot Lasse Kjus, the overall World Cup winner last season but sidelined for much of this one by injury and ailments, took the silver medal in 1:29.89.
Austrian veteran Guenther Mader, 32, made it a memorable day for the old guard with bronze in 1:30.01.

"If this is true, if it's not a dream, I don't think I'll survive today. It's crazy," said a stunned Skaardal, who has not won a World Cup race all season although he finished second in downhills in Chamonix and Val Gardena.
"Maybe because I was more relaxed I could be more aggressive."
Mader was runner-up to Kjus last season in the World Cup and has competed in six world championships.
It was also the sixth bronze medal of his career -- five in world championships and one at the 1992 Olympics.
The Austrian had never won a medal in super-G before.
